newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady to lower, pork bellies mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady to lower, pork bellies mixed.

text.p: CME lean hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent per lb lower while calls ranged from 0.250 cent lower to 0.250 higher for pork belly futures, livestock analysts said.

Steady to lower cash hog indications should prompt carryover pressure in nearby hog contracts. Packers continue to operate at reduced rates and hog runs are adequate for the limited demand, analysts said.
They also noted that cash pork values are only going up slightly despite the reduced kill which indicates slack demand for pork, they added.

Pork bellies were seen continuing their mixed trend with further rolling of long August positions into February despite the stong tone to the current cash belly market linked to reduced hog slaughter, analysts said.

Liquidation should continue in August ahead of its spot position on Friday and concern over deliveries. There is concern that part of the deliverable supply is low grade bellies that more suitable for the trimming market, they said.
Deferred months finished limit up on Wednesday and carryover demand was seen there, sources said.
